input.idea:
samograph.dev — a hosted, fully-managed SaaS wrapping the existing samograph CLI and its Recall.ai meeting bot, so users NEVER run the CLI, manage a Recall token, or set up an ngrok/cloudflared tunnel.

PRODUCT THESIS: samograph is fundamentally about AI agents participating in live meetings. The hosted product's job is to make that turnkey and secure. We ship it in two clearly separated phases.

=== v1 / MVP (this week — the entire build target) ===
Deliberately tiny. The single job: "I sign in, paste a meeting link, and samograph is instantly in my call streaming a live transcript — with zero install, zero token, zero tunnel."
- Marketing + app at samograph.dev.
- Auth: EMAIL MAGIC-LINK ONLY (passwordless). No Google OAuth, no password. Keeps scope minimal and avoids OAuth brand-verification delays.
- One primary action on the dashboard: "Add samograph to a call" — the user pastes a Zoom or Google Meet URL.
- The bot joins immediately. A per-call page streams the LIVE transcript in real time over WebSocket, word-by-word, no reload, no polling. Each line is "[timestamp] Speaker: utterance".
- The live page link is shareable (read-only) so others can follow along (great for hard accents / multilingual / bad audio).
- Transcripts persist to our DB in real time (Recall keeps video only ~7 days; the transcript must be durable and is the product anyway).
- That is ALL. NO calendar, NO AI features in the product UI yet, NO billing, NO video storage, NO summaries. The thesis is that zero-setup + live + persisted already beats Otter/Fireflies/Read/tl;dv for our use case.
- Server-side plumbing the user never sees: ONE shared Recall API key in a secret manager; a MANAGED MULTI-TENANT tunnel (one persistent cloudflared named tunnel per region, NOT one ngrok per call); webhook ingest routed by bot_id; transcript written to Postgres and fanned out to the live WS hub. This is the existing `samograph join` flow refactored to be multi-tenant and server-operated.

=== v2 / Phase 2 (next — the strategic differentiator) ===
SECURE BIDIRECTIONAL AI-AGENT CHANNEL. For an ACTIVE call, the user can mint a scoped, revocable link/token that they paste into an external AI tool (Claude Code, Codex, other agents). Through it the agent gets BIDIRECTIONAL access to that one call:
- LISTEN: subscribe to the live transcript in real time (and recent backfill).
- ACT: the full samograph capability surface, remotely — post in meeting chat, capture frames (frame/frames), set dynamic bot presence (listening/thinking/speaking/acting/idle), and leave. (These map 1:1 to existing samograph CLI verbs.)
So an AI coding agent can sit in a meeting, follow what's said, answer in chat, and look at shared screens — without anyone running the local CLI, token, or tunnel. This is the real reason the product exists.
SECURITY IS THE HARD PART and must be designed up front: per-call capability-scoped tokens (separate read vs act scopes), short TTL tied to call lifetime, one-click revoke, full audit log of every agent action, rate limits on the act channel, and hard tenant isolation — the agent NEVER sees the Recall token, other calls, or other tenants. Abuse model: an agent posting in someone's meeting or grabbing frames must be authorized, logged, and revocable. The channel should be consumable both as a simple HTTP+WebSocket API and ideally as an MCP server endpoint so agents connect natively.

CRITICAL v1 REQUIREMENT: even though the AI channel is Phase 2, v1 architecture MUST leave the seams open for it — a per-call token/capability model, a command/act API in the bot worker (the worker already can chat/frame/presence), per-call auth, capability scoping, and an audit log. Do not paint v1 into a corner that blocks the AI channel.

=== Later (v3+, explicitly deferred) ===
Billing/plans/seats; Google Calendar auto-join; consistent/branded bot identities; post-call transcript email; multi-language UI; long-term video storage + synced transcript+video viewer; MS Teams.

=== Open questions / risks to surface ===
Shared-Recall-token tenant isolation; AI-channel + share-link security and capability scoping; abuse of the act channel; consent/recording disclosure across two-party-consent jurisdictions; Recall.ai per-minute cost guardrails and free-tier rate limits; tunnel as single point of failure (warn into every active call's transcript on outage); magic-link deliverability on corporate mail.

Output the spec organized as user stories with explicit v1 (this week) and v2/Phase-2 (next) sections, an architecture that leaves the AI-channel seams open, a TDD list for the subtle pieces (transcript normalizer, share-token generator, WS fan-out backpressure, tenant-isolation authorization gate, multi-call tunnel watchdog), a team, a sprint plan, and open questions/risks.
